negative_findings.description: Searched in Macedonian and English for a domestic BNPL provider (buy-now-pay-later as a standalone non-bank product).
negative_findings.result_summary: All 'на рати' results were bank-issued interest-free card installment programmes (Stopanska, Komercijalna, NLB) or merchant pages relying on them; no independent MK BNPL fintech surfaced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Suggests installments in MK remain a card-issuer product, so BNPL competitive risk to banks is currently internal rather than from a non-bank challenger — but this needs a second pass with different terms before being asserted.

negative_findings.description: Looked for a licensed crypto-asset exchange or VASP register for North Macedonia.
negative_findings.result_summary: Found only NBRNM crypto Q&A, Ministry of Finance statements that crypto 'will be regulated by law', and FIU material on virtual assets; no register of licensed crypto/e-money crypto firms was located.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Crypto/e-money startups in the cell may be unlicensed or foreign-domiciled, so they will not appear in any MK register and must be tracked via media, app stores and company registry instead.

negative_findings.description: Attempted to locate a corporate/official web presence for 'МКПеј / MKPEJ', reported as preparing the first Macedonian e-wallet.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only secondary press mentions were found; no company site, license entry, or app listing surfaced in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: A potentially significant domestic wallet challenger is currently only traceable via press; needs targeted follow-up in the Central Registry and the NBRNM e-money register.

brief: North Macedonia's non-bank payments landscape is small and unusually legible: a single dominant domestic card processor (CaSys/cPay) sits behind a handful of acquiring banks, and the regulator (NBRNM) publishes registers for e-money institutions, payment institutions and fast-money-transfer providers that together define the challenger universe. The most partnership-revealing sources are not the banks but the intermediaries — CaSys, Monri/Payten, integrator plugin docs — plus the e-commerce association AETM, whose public e-merchant register enumerates merchants with live card acquiring. The clearest recent structural change is the 2025 arrival of the first non-bank EMI (Iute Pay), which makes the NBRNM e-money register a high-frequency watch item, while a second domestic wallet (MKPEJ) remains traceable only through press. Main gaps are company-registry resolution, per-operator remittance mapping, app-store telemetry and Albanian-language coverage.
